We had many people in our comments who assumed we were just random people who bought a tiger cub and many people asking where they can get a tiger. We want to address this because it’s very important. Rick is not just a normal person with a tiger. Rick owns a USDA licensed zoo and Mowgli is not a personal pet. Mowgli came from another zoo and was not purchased as a pet. The reason Mowgli is inside the house (which is on the zoo property) is because he is not fully vaccinated and we will not allow him outside until our vet clears us for that. Anyone who is wanting a pet tiger needs to know that you cannot legally own one as a pet. Also, this is not Rick’s first Tiger. You can go and see Kai, our female, on our page. Rick has extensive experience with big cats and raising them. You can however enjoy how cute he is on our social media! We will NEVER have tiger encounters available and no visitors will ever be allowed to touch him or interact with him. When he is older and cleared to go outside you can see him in his enclosure if you visit the zoo. We hope that clears a few things up!

#TIGER || i have a headache 🤕  1. The vocal repertoire of tigers is vast - they grunt, growl, roar, moan, snarl, chuff, hiss and gasp. It's thought that each vocalisation is used to communicate different things. 2. They are protective over their kill.  Tigers don't usually eat their prey at the kill site - but instead drag their prey into cover to feed. If a tiger leaves - say to get a drink - it will cover it's kill by raking leaves, dirt, grass and even rocks over the carcass. 3. Tigers primarily hunt deer, but as opportunistic predators, they can also eat wild boars, birds, fish, rodents, amphibians, reptiles, and even insects. videos.caption: And if you look at the comments in that video, it’s entirely people saying they want a baby tiger and asking how to get one. Yes, IT IS THIS DEEP.  Any comments calling this out as unethical are swarmed by people saying “this is a wildlife park they know what they’re doing”. People don’t realize that these “wildlife parks” are started up so that people can get the permits to legally own these exotics as pets, and they’ll often use them for profit to have access to more exotics. It’s not a zoo, it’s one persons desire to own tigers and lions and bears as pets and treat them as such, and the messages it sends are incredibly dangerous. Not only that, but NO ethical zoo would ever sell a tiger this young to another zoo, and no ethical zoo would buy a tiger this young from another zoo.  TWP is an unethical facility doing and promoting dangerous things with animals and unfortunately these types of places get a lot of support because the general public wants to play with animals and see cute animal content. If you truly love animals, you know not to support these places no matter how cute their content is, because it’s harming animals.  #zookeeper #animal #animals #animallover #wildlife
